# @moku-labs/editor — full reference

> Editor, devtools and MCP layer for @moku-labs/game, built on @moku-labs/core. Three Moku cores in one package: `editor-agent` (game page), `editor-server` (Bun), `editor-tools` (tools page). One registry of sources and commands feeds the in-game overlay, the tools page and headless tests. The editor reaches the game only through `@moku-labs/game/inspect` and `@moku-labs/game/control` plus the game's `.dev` modules.

This file is the complete machine-readable reference. Every `Config`, `Api` and event payload type below is copied verbatim from `src/config.ts`, `src/plugins/registry/protocol/` and `src/plugins/<name>/types.ts`. The short overview is `llms.txt`; the human overview is `README.md`; detail per plugin is `src/plugins/<name>/README.md`.

Contents:

1. Package and entry points
2. The three cores (`src/config.ts` verbatim)
3. Wire protocol types (verbatim)
4. Error codes
5. Event catalog
6. Configuration reference (type, default, description)
7. Plugins: Config, Api and constants verbatim (17 plugins)
8. Dependency graph and init order
9. Multi-plugin usage examples
10. Writing a custom plugin for each core
11. Wire methods

---

## 1. Package and entry points

- Name: `@moku-labs/editor`, MIT, ESM only (`"type": "module"`).
- Peer dependencies: `@moku-labs/game >= 0.13.1` and `typescript >= 5.5`, both required. The bin's engine page needs `@moku-labs/game/cli` `preparePage` and `watchKeys` (0.13.1). The server opens the game's project index (`@moku-labs/game/project`), which needs `typescript`. Without them the index is off and every view that needs a code location says `Project index is off: <reason>` (see the next item).
- Project index (D-38 … D-48): the server core's `files` plugin opens the project index of its root on start and keeps it fresh with its watch; the tools page asks it through the files-channel `find { key }` (lines read from disk at the call) and reads the key maps from the published `editor.project` state (`link.project()`, event `link:project`). The index is the only source of code locations: Flow node and flow files, the Code tab, Used by, the picked element's JSX and style block, projections, text styles, the asset manifest. A key the index does not know shows `Not in the project index: <key>`; no guess, no crawl. The index needs no `bunfig.toml` (that is only for the hot swap plugin). Moves and edits by agents while the editor is open are followed: open tabs, Used by, Code tab lines, caches.
- Breaking (project index): removed the node → file rule exports (`nodeFile`, `flowFile`, `kebab`, `parseOverrides`, `SOURCE_ROOTS`, `SOURCE_OVERRIDES_PATH`, types `SourceOverrides`) and the protocol file `source-files.ts`; the configs `flowView.stylesFile`, `gameView.manifestPaths`, `gameView.sourceSearch`, `renderView.manifestPaths`; `.moku/editor/files.json` is ignored; the graph node `file` field (F-H2) is gone; `UsedBy.usedIn` is new; `StyleEditCode` gains `"broken"` (no style write while the file does not parse) and `"index-off"` (no style write while the index is off); a key built in a loop answers the element line. `@moku-labs/game >= 0.7.0` and `typescript >= 5.5` are required.
- Doors: game 0.4 replaced `game.rect` with `game.locate` (input `{ key?: string; target?: json }`, answers `Rect | undefined`) and makes `game.capture` answer `{ png: string, legend? }` instead of the data URL itself. The calibration of gameView and renderView reads `{ key }` from `game.locate` when the manifest lists it, else from `game.rect` (`rectSourceOf` in `panels/shared/scene`); with neither, nothing is read, nothing is warned, and the picker says "This game reports no element rects". The capture plugin takes a data URL or an object with a string `png` (`pictureOf`); anything else is still "game.capture gave no picture".
- `files` in the package: `dist`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`. `"sideEffects": false`.
- Production builds: import the agent only inside `if (__MOKU_GAME_DEV__) { await import("@moku-labs/editor/agent") … }`. With the flag defined `false` the bundle keeps no editor code (0 B); with `true` the agent with bridge and capture adds 77.6 KB minified (26.7 KB gzip). The agent core in `src/agent.ts` is created `/* @__PURE__ */`. See README "Production builds" and `tests/integration/agent-bundle.test.ts`.
- Dependencies: `@moku-labs/common`, `@moku-labs/core`, `elkjs`, `preact`.
- Engines: node >= 24, bun >= 1.3.14. The server core and the bin need Bun (`Bun.serve`, HTML imports).
- Bin: `moku-editor` → `./dist/bin.mjs` (source `src/plugins/pages/bin.ts`). Without an html file, in a moku-game folder (`index.ts` + `config.ts`), it serves the engine page: `preparePage` of `@moku-labs/game/cli` with the editor's page agent, the engine's keys watch (`watchKeys` of the same `cli`, in the parent bin until the child exits), then a re-run under `<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml` (see "Engine page" in section 6). It serves with Bun hot reload on (D-23); `--no-hmr` turns it off. `moku-editor mcp` is the stdio MCP server for Claude Code; `moku-editor mcp-config` prints its setup (see "Bin" in section 6).

| Import | File | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| `@moku-labs/editor` | `src/index.ts` | Protocol types (`Json`, `Manifest`, `LinkStatus`, `EditorChannel`, `RunResult`, `WireError`, `SessionInfo`, `ToolsBoot`, `FileEntry`, …), protocol helpers (`checkInput`, `toWireValue`, `encode`, `decode`, `request`, `notification`, `success`, `failure`, `isRequest`, `isResponse`, `isNotification`, `isFailure`, `isJson`, `wireError`, `isWireError`, `toWireError`, `fromWireError`, `isRetryable`, `bareMessage`, `isReloading`, `isHotSwapEntry`, `errorCode`, `ERROR_PREFIX`, `ProtocolError`, `parseProjectState`, `parseFoundList`, `projectDelta`, `firstDefinition`, `anchorKey`), project types (`ProjectState`, `ProjectFound`, `ProjectAnchor`, `ProjectDelta`, `ProjectChange`, `ProjectMove`, `FindParams`), `definePanel`, `SourceValue`, `CompactTools`, `PanelInput`, `PanelSpec`, `PanelTools`, `PanelValues`, `SourceRef`. Runtime-free: no plugin, no core. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/agent` | `src/agent.ts` | `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `registryPlugin`, `channelPlugin`, `overlayPlugin`, `bridgePlugin`, `capturePlugin`, namespaces `Registry`, `Channel`, `Overlay`, `Bridge`, `Capture`. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/agent/page` | `src/agent-page.ts` | Default export only: `editorAgent`, a `PageAgent<Registry.GameLike>` of `@moku-labs/game/app` (D-49). The engine's dev page calls it after the game started with `{ app, name, modules }`: it stops a previous `globalThis.editor`, then `createApp({ plugins: [bridgePlugin, capturePlugin], pluginConfigs: { registry: { game: app, name, modules } } })`, sets `globalThis.editor` and starts it. No side effect on import. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/server` | `src/server.ts` | `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `filesPlugin`, `hubPlugin`, `pagesPlugin`, namespaces `Files`, `Hub`, `Pages`. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/tools` | `src/tools.ts` | `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `linkPlugin`, `workspacePlugin`, `panelsPlugin`, `flowViewPlugin`, `gameViewPlugin`, `renderViewPlugin`, `stateViewPlugin`, `filesViewPlugin`, `consoleViewPlugin`, namespaces `Link`, `Workspace`, `Panels`, `FlowView`, `GameView`, `RenderView`, `StateView`, `FilesView`, `ConsoleView`. |

Default plugins per core (from the entries):

```ts
// src/agent.ts — dependency order: channel and overlay require registry, overlay requires channel.
// Pure: a bundle that uses neither createApp nor createPlugin drops the agent core.
const framework = /* @__PURE__ */ createAgentCore(agentCoreConfig, {
  plugins: [registryPlugin, channelPlugin, overlayPlugin]
});
// opt-in: bridgePlugin, capturePlugin (passed in createApp({ plugins }))

// src/server.ts — dependency order (D-03): files ← hub ← pages.
createServerCore(serverCoreConfig, { plugins: [filesPlugin, hubPlugin, pagesPlugin] });

// src/tools.ts — workspace requires link; panels requires link and workspace; every view
// requires link and panels (all but stateView also workspace). No view depends on another view.
createToolsCore(toolsCoreConfig, {
  plugins: [
    linkPlugin, workspacePlugin, panelsPlugin,
    flowViewPlugin, gameViewPlugin, renderViewPlugin, stateViewPlugin, filesViewPlugin, consoleViewPlugin
  ]
});
```

---

## 2. The three cores (`src/config.ts`, verbatim)

~~~ts
/**
 * @file Framework configuration — three cores in one file (D-01): `editor-agent` for the game
 * page, `editor-server` for the Bun server and `editor-tools` for the tools page. Each core has
 * its own Config and global Events, and registers the core plugins `log` and `env`.
 */
import { envPlugin, logPlugin } from "@moku-labs/common/browser";
import { createCoreConfig } from "@moku-labs/core";
import type { FilesWritten } from "./plugins/files/types";
import type { HubSession } from "./plugins/hub/types";
import type { ElementRef } from "./plugins/panels/shared/scene/types";
import type { LinkStatus, ProjectDelta, ProjectState } from "./plugins/registry/protocol";
import type { Density, RanEvent, WorkspaceId } from "./plugins/workspace/types";

/**
 * Global config of the agent core (the game page). Empty: every option belongs to a plugin.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const config: AgentConfig = {};
 * ```
 */
export type AgentConfig = Record<never, never>;

/**
 * Global config of the server core (Bun). Empty: every option belongs to a plugin.
 */
export type ServerConfig = Record<never, never>;

/**
 * Global config of the tools core (the tools page). Empty: every option belongs to a plugin.
 */
export type ToolsConfig = Record<never, never>;

/**
 * Global events of the agent core. `bridge:status` lives here, not on the bridge, so the overlay
 * hooks it without depending on the opt-in bridge (R2).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("bridge:status", { status: { kind: "live", frame: 12 }, session: "s-7f3a" });
 * ```
 */
export type AgentEvents = {
  /** The bridge link changed kind or session. */
  "bridge:status": { status: LinkStatus; session?: string };
};

/**
 * Global events of the server core (contracts §4).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("files:written", { path: "nodes/merge.ts", bytes: 812, kind: "code" });
 * ```
 */
export type ServerEvents = {
  /** A game session opened (`open: true`) or closed (`open: false`, with a reason). */
  "hub:session": HubSession;
  /** A file was written inside the project root (text or capture). */
  "files:written": FilesWritten;
  /** The project index of the files root opened, changed or went off (hub publishes it). */
  "files:project": ProjectState;
};

/**
 * Global events of the tools core (R4, R9): notices and one-way intents between the tools
 * plugins. Request/response stays in the plugin apis. No view depends on another view.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("workspace:open-file", { path: "nodes/merge.ts", line: 12 });
 * ```
 */
export type ToolsEvents = {
  /** The link status or the chosen session changed. */
  "link:status": { status: LinkStatus; session?: string };
  /** A new project-index state arrived; views drop what the delta names. */
  "link:project": { state: ProjectState; delta: ProjectDelta };
  /** The shown workspace changed. */
  "workspace:changed": { ws: WorkspaceId };
  /** A command run from the tools page settled (top bar, palette, key or a panel's tools.run). */
  "workspace:ran": RanEvent;
  /** The applied density changed (a choice, or `auto` crossing 820 px of window width). */
  "workspace:density": { density: Density };
  /** Reference mode turned on or off (gameView shows its element proxies while on). */
  "workspace:reference": { on: boolean };
  /** Open a file in the Files workspace (filesView hooks it). */
  "workspace:open-file": { path: string; line?: number };
  /** Focus a node in the Flow workspace (flowView hooks it). */
  "workspace:select-node": { id: string };
  /** Focus the edge taken at a frame (flowView hooks it). */
  "workspace:focus-frame": { frame: number };
  /** Select an element in the render tree (renderView hooks it). */
  "workspace:reveal": { ref: ElementRef };
  /** Inspect an element in the Game workspace (gameView hooks it, R9). */
  "workspace:inspect": { ref: ElementRef };
  /** Open a series contact sheet by its index.json path (gameView hooks it). */
  "workspace:open-sheet": { index: string };
};

/**
 * Public API type of a plugin instance, read from its phantom carrier. Mirrors the kernel's
 * non-exported `ExtractPluginApi`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * type Link = ApiOf<typeof linkPlugin>; // the LinkApi type of src/plugins/link/types.ts
 * ```
 */
export type ApiOf<Plugin> = Plugin extends { readonly _phantom: { readonly api: infer PluginApi } }
  ? PluginApi
  : never;

/**
 * Structural type of `ctx.require`, for domain contexts that resolve their own dependencies. The
 * bound repeats the kernel's plugin shape, so the kernel's generic `require` is assignable to it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * type WorkspaceCtx = { readonly require: Require };
 * ```
 */
export type Require = <
  Plugin extends {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly spec: unknown;
    readonly _phantom: {
      readonly config: unknown;
      readonly state: unknown;
      readonly api: unknown;
      readonly events: Record<string, unknown>;
    };
  }
>(
  plugin: Plugin
) => ApiOf<Plugin>;

/**
 * The core plugins every core registers: `ctx.log` and `ctx.env` on every plugin context.
 */
export type CorePlugins = [typeof logPlugin, typeof envPlugin];

const agentConfig: AgentConfig = {};
const serverConfig: ServerConfig = {};
const toolsConfig: ToolsConfig = {};

/**
 * Core config of the agent core (the game page).
 */
export const agentCoreConfig = /* @__PURE__ */ createCoreConfig<
  AgentConfig,
  AgentEvents,
  CorePlugins
>("editor-agent", { config: agentConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin] });

/**
 * Core config of the server core (Bun).
 */
export const serverCoreConfig = /* @__PURE__ */ createCoreConfig<
  ServerConfig,
  ServerEvents,
  CorePlugins
>("editor-server", { config: serverConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin] });

/**
 * Core config of the tools core (the tools page).
 */
export const toolsCoreConfig = /* @__PURE__ */ createCoreConfig<
  ToolsConfig,
  ToolsEvents,
  CorePlugins
>("editor-tools", { config: toolsConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin] });

/**
 * Creates an agent plugin bound to the agent core's Config and Events. Types infer from the spec.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * export const registryPlugin = createAgentPlugin("registry", { config, createState, api });
 * ```
 */
export const createAgentPlugin = agentCoreConfig.createPlugin;

/**
 * Creates a server plugin bound to the server core's Config and Events. Types infer from the spec.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * export const filesPlugin = createServerPlugin("files", { config, createState, api });
 * ```
 */
export const createServerPlugin = serverCoreConfig.createPlugin;

/**
 * Creates a tools plugin bound to the tools core's Config and Events. Types infer from the spec.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * export const linkPlugin = createToolsPlugin("link", { config, createState, api });
 * ```
 */
export const createToolsPlugin = toolsCoreConfig.createPlugin;

/**
 * Creates the agent framework from its core config. Used by `src/agent.ts` only.
 */
export const createAgentCore = agentCoreConfig.createCore;

/**
 * Creates the server framework from its core config. Used by `src/server.ts` only.
 */
export const createServerCore = serverCoreConfig.createCore;

/**
 * Creates the tools framework from its core config. Used by `src/tools.ts` only.
 */
export const createToolsCore = toolsCoreConfig.createCore;
~~~

Each core registers `logPlugin` and `envPlugin` from `@moku-labs/common/browser`: `ctx.log` (leveled events, sinks) and `ctx.env` exist on every plugin context. Plugins log through `ctx.log`, never `console.*`.

---

## 3. Wire protocol types (`src/plugins/registry/protocol/`, verbatim)

The protocol is runtime-free and imports nothing outside itself. It is re-exported from the package root. `project.ts` holds the project-index helpers: `parseProjectState(value)` and `parseFoundList(value)` (strict checked copies, `undefined` for a bad value), `projectDelta(held, next)` (what a view drops: `all: true` after a revision gap, for the first state or an off state; else the lists of `next.change`), `firstDefinition(state, key)` (the first def path of a key, `undefined` when off or unknown) and `anchorKey(ref, path)` (the `style:` or `textStyle:` key of a style block). The project types (`ProjectAnchor`, `ProjectFound`, `ProjectMove`, `ProjectChange`, `ProjectState`, `ProjectDelta`, `FindParams`) mirror the game's `@moku-labs/game/project` types field by field without importing them. `ElementRef` and `PageRect` from `src/plugins/panels/shared/scene/types.ts` (payloads of `workspace:reveal` and `workspace:inspect`). `devices.ts` holds the device presets and their helpers (`DeviceSpec`, `DevicePresetId`, `Orientation`, `DeviceSize` are below); `overlay-host.ts` holds `HOST_ATTRIBUTE`, the DOM marker of the in-game overlay host. `hash.ts` holds `commandsHash(manifest)` (D-37): the commands sorted by id, the JSON of `[id, effect, input]` per command with `input` keys sorted, joined with `\n`, FNV-1a 32-bit, 8 lowercase hex chars; titles and sources do not count. The hub stamps it on `SessionInfo.manifestHash`; the MCP bridge rebuilds its door tools only when it moves. It is in the protocol barrel, not exported from the package root.

~~~ts
/**
 * A JSON value, the way it travels on the wire.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const value: Json = { path: "board/awaitIntent", frame: 1840, tainted: false };
 * ```
 */
export type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };

/**
 * The kind of one input field of a source or a command.
 */
export type InputKind = "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "json";

/**
 * The input of a source or a command: field name to kind; a kind ending in `?` is optional.
 * Structurally identical to the game's InputSchema.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const step: InputSchema = { frames: "number", deltaMs: "number?" };
 * ```
 */
export type InputSchema = Readonly<Record<string, InputKind | `${InputKind}?`>>;

/**
 * How often a source value changes: every frame, on each commit, on each graph edge.
 */
export type Changes = "frame" | "commit" | "edge";

/**
 * What a command does to the game.
 */
export type Effect = "read" | "route" | "cosmetic" | "cheat" | "raw";

/**
 * A source the way the manifest describes it (no functions).
 */
export type SourceDescriptor = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly input: InputSchema;
  readonly changes: Changes;
  /**
   * `false` when the game does not have this source: its door threw on the probe (the game plugin
   * behind it is missing). Reads and watches answer -32008 `not_installed`. Absent = available.
   */
  readonly available?: false;
  /** What the door threw on the probe; present only with `available: false`. */
  readonly reason?: string;
};

/**
 * A command the way the manifest describes it (no functions).
 */
export type CommandDescriptor = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly input: InputSchema;
  readonly effect: Effect;
};

/**
 * What a game page offers the editor: sent by the bridge in `hello`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const manifest: Manifest = { game: "merge-game 0.0.0", page: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/", embedded: true, sources: [], commands: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type Manifest = {
  /** Display name, e.g. "merge-game 0.0.0". */
  readonly game: string;
  /** location.href of the game page. */
  readonly page: string;
  /** True when the page runs inside the tools page frame. */
  readonly embedded: boolean;
  readonly sources: readonly SourceDescriptor[];
  readonly commands: readonly CommandDescriptor[];
  /** Reserved for code-loaded game panels; unused this change. */
  readonly panels?: readonly { readonly id: string; readonly module: string }[];
  /**
   * Set by the bridge in its hello when it restored the checkpoint it stored before Bun's full
   * reload (R6): `bookmark` is the JSON text of the restored `game.bookmark` value, `frame` the
   * frame of the page that took it. Absent on every other hello.
   */
  readonly restored?: { readonly bookmark: string; readonly frame: number };
};

/**
 * Where the game stands after a command.
 */
export type RunState = { readonly path: string; readonly frame: number; readonly tainted: boolean };

/**
 * The answer of a command: its value and the run state.
 */
export type RunResult = { readonly value: Json; readonly state: RunState };

/**
 * One heartbeat of a game page. `heap` is the JS heap of the page in MB, rounded to 0.1, and
 * only present where the browser reports it (Chromium's `performance.memory`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const beat: Heartbeat = { frame: 1840, paused: false, at: 1790000000000, heap: { usedMb: 12.8, limitMb: 4095.8 } };
 * ```
 */
export type Heartbeat = {
  readonly frame: number;
  readonly paused: boolean;
  /** Epoch ms of the beat. */
  readonly at: number;
  readonly heap?: { readonly usedMb: number; readonly limitMb: number };
};

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `tap` notification: one pointerdown on the game page. `x` and `y`
 * are page CSS px of the game document (`clientX`, `clientY`); `at` is the page's
 * `performance.now()`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const tap: Tap = { x: 206, y: 640, at: 15234.5 };
 * ```
 */
export type Tap = { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; readonly at: number };

/**
 * The link state shown everywhere (design-context §6 B1, F3). A `lost` with `reloading: true` is
 * an expected reload (U7): a server restart (close 1012), a reload the editor started, or a game
 * that said bye before its reload. The views show it in a neutral tone until the game is back, or
 * as a plain `lost` once link's `reloadGraceMs` ran out.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const status: LinkStatus = { kind: "live", frame: 1840 };
 * const reloading: LinkStatus = { kind: "lost", reason: "socket_closed", lastFrame: 1825, retryInMs: 1000, reloading: true };
 * ```
 */
export type LinkStatus =
  | { kind: "connecting" }
  | { kind: "live"; frame: number }
  | { kind: "paused"; frame: number }
  | { kind: "silent"; since: number; lastFrame: number }
  | { kind: "lost"; reason: string; lastFrame: number; retryInMs: number; reloading?: true }
  | { kind: "empty" };

/**
 * The channel every panel reads through: in process (`app.channel`, the agent channel of the game
 * page) or remote (`app.link`, the tools link to the editor server). The base of `ChannelApi` and
 * `LinkApi`. Errors reject as wire errors: -32601 `unknown_id`, -32602 `invalid_input`, the
 * command's own error; the remote link adds its transport reasons (`timeout`, `link_closed` …).
 */
export type EditorChannel = {
  /**
   * Reads a source now.
   *
   * @param id - The source id, e.g. "game.position".
   * @param input - The source input; omit it for a source without input.
   * @returns A promise of the wire value. It never throws synchronously.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A panel shows where the game stands.
   * await app.channel.read("game.position"); // { path: "home", … }
   * await app.channel.read("game.history", { last: 1 }); // [{ path: "home", outcome: "play", … }]
   * ```
   */
  read(id: string, input?: Json): Promise<Json>;
  /**
   * Follows a source: delivers the current value first, then every change.
   *
   * @param id - The source id.
   * @param input - The source input; `undefined` means none, but the argument is required.
   * @param onValue - Called with each value.
   * @returns An idempotent stop.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The state view follows the position until the view closes.
   * const stop = app.channel.watch("game.position", undefined, position => show(position));
   * stop();
   * ```
   */
  watch(id: string, input: Json | undefined, onValue: (value: Json) => void): () => void;
  /**
   * Runs a command. The in-process channel runs it in a microtask, off the game's frame loop.
   *
   * @param id - The command id, e.g. "game.step".
   * @param input - The command input; omit it for a command without input.
   * @returns A promise of the command's value and where the game stands after it.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The flow view steps one frame.
   * (await app.channel.run("game.step", { frames: 1 })).state; // { path: "home", frame: 1841, tainted: false }
   * ```
   */
  run(id: string, input?: Json): Promise<RunResult>;
  /**
   * The link state now. The in-process channel answers live or paused only.
   *
   * @returns A fresh LinkStatus.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.channel.status(); // { kind: "live", frame: 1840 }
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).status(); // { kind: "silent", since: 1790000000000, lastFrame: 1840 }
   * ```
   */
  status(): LinkStatus;
};

/**
 * The logical channel of a wire message.
 */
export type Channel = "game" | "files" | "editor";

/**
 * Why a call failed (R1 adds `link_closed`). The selection relay adds `no_editor_page` (-32003: no
 * tools page with `role=page` is open) and `page_closed` (-32001, retryable: the page closed before
 * it answered).
 */
export type ErrorReason =
  | "game_reloaded"
  | "no_session"
  | "choose_session"
  | "timeout"
  | "invalid_input"
  | "unknown_id"
  | "command_failed"
  | "not_json"
  | "forbidden_path"
  | "version_conflict"
  | "unauthorized"
  | "not_installed"
  | "link_closed"
  | "no_editor_page"
  | "page_closed";

/**
 * A JSON-RPC error object with the editor's data fields.
 */
export type WireError = {
  code: number;
  message: string;
  data?: { retryable?: boolean; reason?: ErrorReason; id?: string; field?: string };
};

/**
 * A request: carries an id and gets exactly one response.
 */
export type Request = {
  jsonrpc: "2.0";
  id: number;
  channel: Channel;
  method: string;
  params?: Json;
  session?: string;
};

/**
 * The response to a request: a result or an error.
 */
export type Response =
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: number; result: Json }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: number; error: WireError };

/**
 * A notification: no id, no response.
 */
export type Notification = {
  jsonrpc: "2.0";
  channel: Channel;
  method: string;
  params?: Json;
  session?: string;
};

/**
 * One game session the way a tools client sees it: the five R1 fields, the hub's liveness readout
 * once the game has sent a heartbeat (M4), and the hash of the session's command doors (D-37).
 * Old clients ignore `heartbeat` and `manifestHash`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // A paused game in the editor pane, as moku_sessions lists it.
 * const info: SessionInfo = {
 *   id: "s-7f3a",
 *   game: "merge-game 0.0.0",
 *   page: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/",
 *   embedded: true,
 *   connectedAt: 1790000000000,
 *   heartbeat: { frame: 1840, paused: true, silent: false },
 *   manifestHash: "4f528e73"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type SessionInfo = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly game: string;
  readonly page: string;
  readonly embedded: boolean;
  /** Epoch ms. */
  readonly connectedAt: number;
  /**
   * Frame and paused of the last heartbeat, and the hub's silent flag. Absent before the first
   * heartbeat. The hub re-sends the list when paused or silent flips, not on every frame.
   */
  readonly heartbeat?: {
    readonly frame: number;
    readonly paused: boolean;
    readonly silent: boolean;
  };
  /**
   * `commandsHash` of the session's manifest, set by the hub on hello. The MCP bridge compares it
   * to rebuild its door tools only when the commands change. Absent from an old hub.
   */
  readonly manifestHash?: string;
};

/**
 * One child of a folder in the files channel.
 */
export type FileEntry = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly kind: "file" | "dir";
  readonly size: number;
  readonly version?: string;
};

/**
 * A text file and its version (sha1 of the bytes).
 */
export type FileText = { readonly text: string; readonly version: string };

/**
 * An image read back in a data URL, with its version.
 */
export type FileBinary = { readonly dataUrl: string; readonly version: string };

/**
 * The result of a write.
 */
export type WriteResult = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly bytes: number;
  readonly version: string;
};

/**
 * Body of `GET {path}/hello`. The socket URL is `{path}/ws?token=<t>&kind=agent|tools` (R1); `ws`
 * carries it without the query.
 */
export type HelloBody = { readonly ws: string; readonly token: string };

/**
 * The JSON of `#moku-editor-boot` in the tools page (R1, R3).
 */
export type ToolsBoot = {
  readonly v: 1;
  /** Socket URL without the query. */
  readonly ws: string;
  readonly token: string;
  /** The hub path, e.g. "/__editor". */
  readonly path: string;
  readonly title: string;
  /** "Open in editor" template, unexpanded. */
  readonly editorUrl: string;
  /** Absolute real project root. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** Same-origin URL of the game page. */
  readonly gameUrl: string;
};

/**
 * A device preset of the tools page (R1, R4): the screen in CSS px, its pixel ratio, safe insets,
 * corner radius, the `<optgroup>` it is listed under and the frame drawn around it (R9). A foldable
 * adds its two screens; its top-level size is the cover screen.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const iphone15: DeviceSpec = {
 *   id: "iphone-15", name: "iPhone 15", w: 393, h: 852, safeTop: 59, safeBottom: 34, kind: "phone",
 *   dpr: 3, radius: 55, group: "iphone", frame: "modern"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceSpec = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
  readonly safeTop: number;
  readonly safeBottom: number;
  readonly kind: "phone" | "tablet" | "desktop";
  /** Device pixel ratio of the screen. */
  readonly dpr: number;
  /** Corner radius of the screen in CSS px (0 for a desktop). */
  readonly radius: number;
  /** The `<optgroup>` the preset is listed under. */
  readonly group: "iphone" | "android" | "foldable" | "tablet" | "desktop";
  /**
   * The frame drawn around the screen (R9): "modern" is the thin bezel every current device has;
   * "home-button" is the iPhone SE look, with 64 px bands above and below the screen and a round
   * home button in the bottom one.
   */
  readonly frame: "modern" | "home-button";
  /** Set when a value of the preset is an estimate, not a published figure. */
  readonly approx?: true;
  /** The two screens of a foldable: folded (cover) and unfolded (inner). */
  readonly fold?: { readonly cover: FoldScreen; readonly inner: FoldScreen };
};

/**
 * The twenty-one device presets (round 2 R4, round 2b R10), in display order.
 */
export type DevicePresetId =
  | "iphone-se"
  | "iphone-15"
  | "iphone-17e"
  | "iphone-air"
  | "iphone-18-pro"
  | "iphone-18-pro-max"
  | "iphone-15-pro-max"
  | "iphone-16-pro"
  | "iphone-16-pro-max"
  | "galaxy-s24"
  | "galaxy-a55"
  | "redmi-note-13"
  | "pixel-8"
  | "xperia-1-v"
  | "galaxy-z-fold-6"
  | "galaxy-z-flip-6"
  | "pixel-9-pro-fold"
  | "iphone-duo"
  | "ipad-mini"
  | "ipad-air-11"
  | "desktop";

/**
 * Device orientation.
 */
export type Orientation = "portrait" | "landscape";

/**
 * Size and safe insets of a preset in an orientation (resolveDevice, R8).
 */
export type DeviceSize = {
  w: number;
  h: number;
  safe: { top: number; right: number; bottom: number; left: number };
};

/**
 * The prefix of every error message the editor throws or returns (R1, R7).
 */
export const ERROR_PREFIX = "[moku-editor] ";

/**
 * JSON-RPC error codes of the editor (contracts §2, R6). The selection relay reuses two codes
 * under its own names: `noEditorPage` (-32003, reason `no_editor_page`) and `pageClosed` (-32001,
 * reason `page_closed`, retryable).
 */
export const errorCode = {
  invalidRequest: -32_600,
  unknownMethod: -32_601,
  invalidInput: -32_602,
  commandFailed: -32_000,
  gameReloaded: -32_001,
  timeout: -32_002,
  noSession: -32_003,
  forbiddenPath: -32_004,
  versionConflict: -32_005,
  notJson: -32_006,
  unauthorized: -32_007,
  notInstalled: -32_008,
  noEditorPage: -32_003,
  pageClosed: -32_001
} as const;

/**
 * Any wire message.
 */
export type Message = Request | Response | Notification;

/**
 * A subscription id on the wire: a safe integer ≥ 0 on both hops (R6).
 */
export type SubId = number; // eslint-disable-line sonarjs/redundant-type-aliases -- R6 names the wire subscription id

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `read` request.
 */
export type ReadParams = { id: string; input?: Json };

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `read` request.
 */
export type ReadParams = { id: string; input?: Json };

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `watch` request.
 */
export type WatchParams = { sub: SubId; id: string; input?: Json };

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `unwatch` request.
 */
export type UnwatchParams = { sub: SubId };

/**
 * Params of the game-channel `run` request.
 */
export type RunParams = { id: string; input?: Json };

/**
 * Params of the agent's first notification.
 */
export type HelloParams = { manifest: Manifest };

/**
 * Params of a `value` notification.
 */
export type ValueParams = { sub: SubId; value: Json };

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel `session` notification (= the hub's HubSession; also sent to the
 * agent right after its hello, R6).
 */
export type SessionParams = {
  id: string;
  game: string;
  open: boolean;
  reason?: "bye" | "game_reloaded";
};

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel `sessions` notification.
 */
export type SessionsParams = { list: SessionInfo[] };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `list` request.
 */
export type ListParams = { dir: string };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `read` and `readBinary` requests.
 */
export type PathParams = { path: string };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `write` request.
 */
export type WriteParams = { path: string; text: string; version?: string };

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `writeBinary` request (`data` is a data URL, R1).
 */
export type WriteBinaryParams = { path: string; data: string };

/**
 * A graph node by flow and node name: the `node:<flow>/<node>` key of the project index.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // filesView's Used by card lists the nodes a file defines.
 * const ref: NodeRef = { flow: "board", node: "merge" }; // node:board/merge
 * ```
 */
export type NodeRef = { readonly flow: string; readonly node: string };

/**
 * Where a project-index key is defined or used, without a line: the file and what in it holds the
 * key. Mirrors the game's `Anchor` (`@moku-labs/game/project`) field by field.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // node:board/merge, defined by the const `merge` of nodes/merge.ts.
 * const anchor: ProjectAnchor = { path: "nodes/merge.ts", binding: "merge" };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectAnchor = {
  /** The file, root-relative POSIX. */
  readonly path: string;
  /** The const, function or export the definition is bound to. */
  readonly binding?: string;
  /** The property or attribute key: a text style key, the `name` of a projection, a JSX key. */
  readonly key?: string;
  /**
   * JSX: the component a key-carrying prop sits on, or the component a `{id}` or `{amountKey}`
   * pattern is written in.
   */
  readonly component?: string;
  /** JSX only: how the key is written. */
  readonly kind?: "literal" | "template" | "idProp" | "ident";
  /** JSX templates and identifiers: the literal head of the pattern, `card` for `card*Picture`. */
  readonly stem?: string;
  /** JSX idProp: the prop the value sits on, `id` or `amountKey`. */
  readonly prop?: string;
};

/**
 * One answer of the files-channel `find`: the anchor with its line read from disk at the call.
 * Mirrors the game's `Found`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The JSX key settingsBoard: the line of its attribute, the whole element as the range.
 * const found: ProjectFound = {
 *   path: "features/settings/settings.tsx",
 *   key: "settingsBoard",
 *   component: "Signboard",
 *   kind: "idProp",
 *   prop: "id",
 *   line: 290,
 *   range: [289, 7, 310, 19],
 *   hash: "0f3c9a…"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectFound = ProjectAnchor & {
  /** The line, 1-based. */
  readonly line: number;
  /** Start line, start column, end line, end column; 1-based, the end column exclusive. */
  readonly range: readonly [
    startLine: number,
    startColumn: number,
    endLine: number,
    endColumn: number
  ];
  /** sha1 hex of the bytes the line was read from; equals the files `version` of those bytes. */
  readonly hash: string;
  /** The file does not parse now; the line comes from its last good parse. Write no style edit. */
  readonly broken?: true;
};

/**
 * A project-index key that left one file for another in one watch batch.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const move: ProjectMove = {
 *   key: "node:board/catchUp",
 *   from: "nodes/catch-up.ts",
 *   to: "nodes/board/catch-up.ts"
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectMove = { readonly key: string; readonly from: string; readonly to: string };

/**
 * What one watch batch of the project index changed. The game's `ProjectChange` without its
 * `revision`, which `ProjectState` carries.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // An agent moved nodes/catch-up.ts into nodes/board/ and fixed the import of the board flow.
 * const change: ProjectChange = {
 *   files: ["flows/board.ts", "nodes/board/catch-up.ts", "nodes/catch-up.ts"],
 *   moved: [{ key: "node:board/catchUp", from: "nodes/catch-up.ts", to: "nodes/board/catch-up.ts" }],
 *   removed: []
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectChange = {
  /** The root-relative paths whose bytes changed, appeared or vanished, sorted. */
  readonly files: readonly string[];
  readonly moved: readonly ProjectMove[];
  /** Keys gone from every file. */
  readonly removed: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * The project index as the server publishes it (`editor.project`): `off` with the reason, or
 * `on` with the key → path maps. JSX keys never ride the state; only `find` reaches them.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const off: ProjectState = { state: "off", reason: "disabled" };
 * const on: ProjectState = {
 *   state: "on",
 *   revision: "9c1e…",
 *   manifest: "manifest.json",
 *   defs: { "flow:board": ["flows/board.ts"], "node:board/merge": ["nodes/merge.ts"] },
 *   uses: { "node:board/merge": ["flows/board.ts"] },
 *   broken: {}
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectState =
  | { readonly state: "off"; readonly reason: string }
  | {
      readonly state: "on";
      readonly revision: string;
      /** Revision before this batch; absent on the first state after open. */
      readonly previous?: string;
      /** The asset manifest, root-relative, when that file exists. */
      readonly manifest?: string;
      /** Every key except `jsx:` → its def paths, in def order (a conflict lists both). */
      readonly defs: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
      /** `node:` and `style:` keys that have uses → the paths of the uses. */
      readonly uses: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
      /** Broken files → the first parse error (`<path>:<line>:<col> <message>`). */
      readonly broken: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
      /** What the batch behind this state changed; absent on the first state after open. */
      readonly change?: ProjectChange;
    };

/**
 * What a view drops when a new project state arrives: `all` after a revision gap (reconnect, the
 * first state, off), otherwise the files, moves and removed keys of the batch.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const delta: ProjectDelta = { all: false, files: ["nodes/merge.ts"], moved: [], removed: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type ProjectDelta = {
  readonly all: boolean;
  readonly files: readonly string[];
  readonly moved: readonly ProjectMove[];
  readonly removed: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * Params of the files-channel `find` request: one project-index key.
 */
export type FindParams = { key: string };

/**
 * A ui element by its path of segments, or a world entity by id.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const ref: ElementRef = { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" };
 * ```
 */
export type ElementRef =
  | { readonly kind: "ui"; readonly path: string }
  | { readonly kind: "entity"; readonly id: number };

/**
 * A rect in CSS px of the game page (the iframe viewport = device W×H).
 */
export type PageRect = {
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
};

/**
 * The size and corner radius of one screen of a foldable device, in CSS px.
 */
export type FoldScreen = { readonly w: number; readonly h: number; readonly radius: number };

/**
 * The hot reload state of the game server (R6): Bun HMR on or off, and who owns the server. The
 * hub sends it to every tools page as the editor-channel notification `hotReload`, and again
 * after each tools connection opens.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const state: HotReload = { hmr: true, owner: "bin" };
 * ```
 */
export type HotReload = {
  /** True when Bun reloads the game page on a source change. */
  readonly hmr: boolean;
  /** "bin" when the moku-editor bin serves the game, "server" for a game's own Bun.serve. */
  readonly owner: "bin" | "server";
};

/**
 * A selected element: a ui element by its path, or a world entity by id. The same shape as the
 * scene's `ElementRef` (panels/shared/scene), declared here so the wire module imports nothing.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const ref: SelectionRef = { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionRef =
  | { readonly kind: "ui"; readonly path: string }
  | { readonly kind: "entity"; readonly id: number };

/**
 * A rect in CSS px of the game page (the iframe viewport). The same shape as the scene's `PageRect`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const rect: SelectionRect = { x: 12, y: 40, w: 96, h: 24 };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionRect = {
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
};

/**
 * One element of an area selection (U9): the group roots that lie in the area, in page order.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const item: SelectionItem = {
 *   ref: { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" },
 *   key: "coins",
 *   name: "coins",
 *   type: "text",
 *   rect: { x: 12, y: 40, w: 96, h: 24 },
 *   source: { path: "src/ui/hud.ts", line: 42 }
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionItem = {
  readonly ref: SelectionRef;
  /** The ui node's `key`, when it has one. */
  readonly key?: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: string;
  /** Where it is drawn, in page CSS px. Absent: not placed. */
  readonly rect?: SelectionRect;
  /** The style source line of the element, once found. */
  readonly source?: { readonly path: string; readonly line: number };
};

/**
 * The element selected in the editor page, as the page publishes it (editor-channel notification
 * `selection`) and as the hub answers `editor.selection` and `editor.select`. Check a received
 * value with `parseSelectionInfo`. Its readonly `items` make it not assignable to the mutable
 * Json: senders pass it through `toWireValue`, like a Manifest.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The picker landed on the coins label; the card and the crop are written.
 * const info: SelectionInfo = {
 *   ref: { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" },
 *   key: "coins",
 *   projection: "hud",
 *   name: "coins",
 *   type: "text",
 *   rect: { x: 12, y: 40, w: 96, h: 24 },
 *   source: { path: "src/ui/hud.ts", line: 42 },
 *   card: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/coins-f1840.md",
 *   crop: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/coins-f1840-crop.jpg",
 *   line: "@moku coins text · src/ui/hud.ts:42 · .moku/captures/2026-10-05/coins-f1840.md",
 *   session: "s-7f3a",
 *   frame: 1840,
 *   at: 1790000000000
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type SelectionInfo = {
  readonly ref: SelectionRef;
  /** The ui node's `key`, when it has one. */
  readonly key?: string;
  /** The projection the element belongs to, e.g. "hud". */
  readonly projection?: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: string;
  /** Where it is drawn, in page CSS px (as `SceneNode.rect`). Absent: not placed. */
  readonly rect?: SelectionRect;
  /** The style source line of the element, once found. */
  readonly source?: { readonly path: string; readonly line: number };
  /** The capture card, project-relative under `capturesDir`. Set after a pick. */
  readonly card?: string;
  /** The element crop picture, project-relative under `capturesDir`. Set after a pick. */
  readonly crop?: string;
  /** The one-line `@moku …` reference of the element. */
  readonly line?: string;
  /** The game session the element belongs to. */
  readonly session?: string;
  /** The scene frame; after a pick the frame of the pick. */
  readonly frame?: number;
  /**
   * The area of an area selection (U9), in page CSS px. An area selection has `type: "area"`,
   * `name: "area"`, `rect` = the area and `ref` = the first item's ref (`{ kind: "ui", path: "" }`
   * when no element is inside).
   */
  readonly area?: SelectionRect;
  /** The elements of an area selection, top to bottom then left to right; at most 40. */
  readonly items?: readonly SelectionItem[];
  /** Epoch ms of the publish (`Date.now()`). */
  readonly at: number;
};

/**
 * The value of each method `publish` sends to the tools pages (A5): the hub keeps the last one
 * per method and replays it to every tools connection that opens.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const kept: PublishParams = {
 *   hotReload: { hmr: true, owner: "bin" },
 *   selection: null,
 *   project: { state: "off", reason: "not opened" }
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type PublishParams = {
  readonly hotReload: HotReload;
  /** `null`: nothing is selected. */
  readonly selection: SelectionInfo | null;
  /** The project index of the files root (`files:project`). */
  readonly project: ProjectState;
};

/**
 * A method `publish` sends to the tools pages (R6): `"hotReload"`, `"selection"` or `"project"`.
 */
export type PublishMethod = keyof PublishParams;

/**
 * The format a picture travels in on the wire (editor.capture, editor.sheet, a crop): `"jpeg"`
 * (the default, D-34) or `"png"` (lossless).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const format: PictureFormat = "jpeg";
 * ```
 */
export type PictureFormat = "jpeg" | "png";

/**
 * Params of the editor-channel request `select`: an area by `rect`, the element by `key` (a ui
 * node key, projection-qualified like `"hud/infoBar"` allowed) or by `ref`. `rect` wins over `key`
 * and `ref`. `card` (the page treats absent
 * as true) asks for the capture card and the crop as after a picker click.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const params: SelectParams = { key: "hud/infoBar", card: true };
 * const areaParams: SelectParams = { rect: { x: 0, y: 30, w: 200, h: 60 } }; // every element inside
 * ```
 */
export type SelectParams = {
  readonly key?: string;
  readonly ref?: SelectionRef;
  /** An area in page CSS px, picked like a Reference-mode drag (U9). It wins over key and ref. */
  readonly rect?: SelectionRect;
  readonly card?: boolean;
};

/**
 * The editor-channel notifications by method, with their params. `session` goes to agents and
 * tools, the rest to tools connections. `selection` is also sent by the editor page (a tools
 * connection with `role=page`) to the hub.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const note: EditorNotifications["selection"] = null; // nothing is selected
 * ```
 */
export type EditorNotifications = {
  readonly session: SessionParams;
  readonly sessions: SessionsParams;
} & PublishParams;

/**
 * The name of an editor-channel notification.
 */
export type EditorNotificationMethod = keyof EditorNotifications;

/**
 * The editor-channel requests by method: `selection` (answered by the hub with the last published
 * selection) and `select` (relayed by the hub to the editor page, which answers the selection).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const answer: EditorRequests["select"]["result"] = info; // the element after the select
 * ```
 */
export type EditorRequests = {
  readonly selection: {
    readonly params: Readonly<Record<string, never>>;
    readonly result: SelectionInfo | null;
  };
  readonly select: { readonly params: SelectParams; readonly result: SelectionInfo };
};

/**
 * The name of an editor-channel request.
 */
export type EditorRequestMethod = keyof EditorRequests;
~~~

---

## 4. Error codes

All errors are JSON-RPC error objects (`WireError`). Messages start with `[moku-editor] ` (`ERROR_PREFIX`). No stack crosses the wire. `bareMessage(message)` strips the prefix for UI text.

| Code | `errorCode` key | `data.reason` | Retryable | Raised by | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -32600 | `invalidRequest` | — | no | hub | duplicate `sub` on one connection; more than 256 pending calls per tools connection |
| -32601 | `unknownMethod` | `unknown_id` (with `data.id`) or none | no | channel, bridge, hub, files, capture | unknown source or command id; unknown channel or method; missing file or folder (`files`) |
| -32602 | `invalidInput` | `invalid_input` (`data.field`) | no | registry, capture, hub, files | input fails `checkInput`; bad `sub`; text over 2 MiB or binary over 16 MiB on write; bad data URL |
| -32000 | `commandFailed` | `command_failed` | no | registry, capture, hub, files | a door threw; `game.capture` gave no picture; a series is already recording; IO error; file too large on read |
| -32001 | `gameReloaded` | `game_reloaded` | yes | hub | the agent closed while a call was pending |
| -32001 | `pageClosed` | `page_closed` | yes | hub | the editor page closed before it answered a relayed `editor.select` |
| -32002 | `timeout` | `timeout` | yes | bridge, hub, link | the call passed its deadline (the command is not cancelled) |
| -32002 | `timeout` | `link_closed` | yes | link | socket not open, socket closed, or `app.stop()` |
| -32003 | `noSession` | `no_session` | no | hub, link | no game connected, or the named session is not open |
| -32003 | `noSession` | `choose_session` | no | hub, link | several sessions and not exactly one embedded; `link.choose` with an id that is not open |
| -32003 | `noEditorPage` | `no_editor_page` | no | hub | `editor.select` and no tools connection with `role=page` is open ("Open the editor page: <url>") |
| -32004 | `forbiddenPath` | `forbidden_path` | no | files | a path fails a sandbox rule |
| -32005 | `versionConflict` | `version_conflict` | no | files | stale `version`, or a `version` for a missing file |
| -32006 | `notJson` | `not_json` | no | registry (`toWireValue`) | a value is not JSON (function, symbol, bigint, cycle, depth over 64) |
| -32007 | `unauthorized` | `unauthorized` | no | hub | a request from an agent connection |
| -32008 | `notInstalled` | `not_installed` (with `data.id`) | no | registry | a read or watch of a source the game does not have: its door threw on the probe (manifest `available: false`). Message `[moku-editor] source <id> is not available in this game: <reason>`. The link does not log or retry it. |

Deadlines: bridge `callTimeoutMs` (5000), hub `callTimeoutMs` (5000), link `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (10000). A `run` of `editor.series` gets `min(input.durationMs, 60000)` on top in all three, and a `run` of `editor.sheet` gets `min(input.frames × input.everyMs, 60000)`. The MCP bridge waits at most 70 s for any hub answer.

Config errors (not wire errors) are thrown at `createApp` from `onInit`, in the shape:

```
[moku-editor] <plugin>.<field> <problem>.
  <fix line, e.g. Pass pluginConfigs.channel.heartbeatMs, for example 1000.>
```

Examples: `[moku-editor] registry.game is missing.`, `[moku-editor] registry.game is not a game app.`, `[moku-editor] Duplicate registry id "<id>".`, `[moku-editor] files.root "<root>" is not a directory.`, `[moku-editor] files.allow is empty.`, `[moku-editor] Panel "<id>" is already registered.`, `[moku-editor] Key "<combo>" is already bound in <scope>.`

Websocket close codes: 1000 normal (bridge `bye`, link stop), 1001 `editor stopping` (hub stop), 1003 binary frame, 1008 `hello first` / `bad manifest` / `hello twice` / ten malformed messages, 1009 frame over 32 MiB (Bun).

Upgrade refusals of `hub.fetch` (in check order): 404 `missing`, 503 `unavailable`, 426 `upgrade`, 403 `forbidden`, 401 `unauthorized`, 400 `invalid`.

---

## 5. Event catalog

Global events only; no plugin declares its own `events` field. Payload types are in section 2 (`AgentEvents`, `ServerEvents`, `ToolsEvents`) and sections 3 and 7.

| Core | Event | Payload type | Emitted by | When | Hooked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent | `bridge:status` | `{ status: LinkStatus; session?: string }` | bridge | at start (`connecting`), on every change of status kind, on every session change; never from `onStop` | overlay (link dot) |
| server | `hub:session` | `HubSession` | hub | a valid `hello` (`open: true`); an agent close (`open: false`, `reason` `"bye"` or `"game_reloaded"`) | none in the package; for consumer plugins |
| server | `files:written` | `FilesWritten` | files | after each successful `write` or `writeBinary`, after the rename; `kind` from `classifyWrite(path)` | none in the package; for consumer plugins |
| server | `files:project` | `ProjectState` | files | the project index opened (on), a watch batch changed it (on, with `previous` and `change`), or it went off (once) | hub (`publish("project", state)`: the `editor.project` notification, kept and replayed) |
| tools | `link:status` | `{ status: LinkStatus; session?: string }` | link | status changed kind or any field, or the session changed | workspace, panels, flowView, gameView, renderView, stateView, filesView, consoleView |
| tools | `link:project` | `{ state: ProjectState; delta: ProjectDelta }` | link | a new `editor.project` state: not the held one again (on at the same revision and manifest, off with the same reason). `delta` is `projectDelta(held, next)`; at the same revision with another `manifest` it is `{ all: false, files: [old, new manifest] }` | flowView, gameView, renderView, filesView |
| tools | `workspace:changed` | `{ ws: WorkspaceId }` | workspace | `show()` changed the workspace | panels, flowView, gameView, renderView, filesView |
| tools | `workspace:ran` | `RanEvent` | workspace (origins `topbar`, `key`, `palette`), panels (origin `panel`, or the api `run` origin) | a command run from the tools page settled | stateView (taint), consoleView (error lines) |
| tools | `workspace:density` | `{ density: Density }` (`"compact" \| "comfortable"`) | workspace | the applied density changed: a choice in the palette, or `auto` crossing 820 px of window width | flowView (ELK spacing) |
| tools | `workspace:reference` | `{ on: boolean }` | workspace | Reference mode turned on or off (key R, the top-bar target button, `setReference`) | gameView (element proxies) |
| tools | `workspace:open-file` | `{ path: string; line?: number }` | flowView, gameView | "Open in Files" | filesView |
| tools | `workspace:select-node` | `{ id: string }` | filesView | a Used-by chip | flowView |
| tools | `workspace:focus-frame` | `{ frame: number }` | consoleView | a frame link, `focusFrame()` | flowView |
| tools | `workspace:reveal` | `{ ref: ElementRef }` | gameView | "Show in render tree" | renderView |
| tools | `workspace:inspect` | `{ ref: ElementRef }` | renderView | "Inspect in Game" | gameView |
| tools | `workspace:open-sheet` | `{ index: string }` | filesView | "Open contact sheet" on a series `index.json` | gameView |

`files:written` kind rules (`classifyWrite`, first match wins): starts with `.moku/captures/` → `capture`; equals `.moku/editor/layout.json` → `layout`; ends with `.css`, basename `styles.ts`/`styles.tsx`, ends with `.styles.ts`/`.styles.tsx`, or a `.ts`/`.tsx` module directly in a `styles/` folder (`shared/styles/text.ts`) → `style`; other `.ts`/`.tsx` → `code`; else `other`.

`LinkStatus` semantics: `connecting` (socket open or session attached, no heartbeat yet); `live`/`paused` (the chosen session beats; `paused` from the heartbeat flag); `silent` (no heartbeat for 6 s, or 65 s after a `paused: true` beat); `lost` (socket closed, chosen session closed, or no boot tag `no_boot`); `empty` (connected, no game session, also 10 s after a lost session). The bridge reports only `connecting`, `live`, `paused`, `lost`.

Not events: heartbeats are a callback api (`channel.onHeartbeat`), and so are taps (`link.onTap`); `ctx.log` lines such as `hub:refused`, `bridge:lost`, `registry:watch-failed`, `registry:source-unavailable`, `link:watch-failed`, `panels:view-failed` are log events, listed in each plugin README.

---

## 6. Configuration reference

All options are set per plugin through `createApp({ pluginConfigs: { <plugin>: { … } } })`, shallow-merged over the defaults (arrays replace). Global configs are empty. Bad values throw at `createApp`.

### Agent

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| registry | `game` | `GameLike \| undefined` | `undefined` | Required. The app the game made with `createApp`. `onInit` throws without it. |
| registry | `modules` | `readonly DevModule[]` | `[]` | The game's `.dev` modules: extra sources and commands, added after the doors. |
| registry | `name` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | `Manifest.game`. Falls back to trimmed `document.title`, then `"game"`. |
| channel | `heartbeatMs` | `number` | `1000` | Ms between two beats. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| overlay | `open` | `boolean` | `false` | Open at start. A QA build sets `true`. |
| overlay | `corner` | `Corner` | `"top-right"` | `"top-right" \| "top-left" \| "bottom-right" \| "bottom-left"`. |
| overlay | `mount` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | CSS selector of the element the host is appended to; `undefined` = `document.body`. |
| bridge | `hello` | `string` | `"/__editor/hello"` | Hello route: same-origin path or absolute URL. Non-empty. |
| bridge | `retryMs` | `number` | `1000` | First reconnect delay; doubles per failure up to `MAX_RETRY_MS` (30000), ±20 % jitter. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| bridge | `callTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Deadline of one `read` or `run`. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| capture | `maxDurationMs` | `number` | `20000` | Longest series accepted. More → -32602 field `durationMs`. |
| capture | `minIntervalMs` | `number` | `16` | Shortest interval accepted. Less → -32602 field `intervalMs`. |

### Server

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| files | `root` | `string` | `"."` | Project root, absolute or relative to the working folder. Resolved once with `realpathSync`; must be an existing folder. |
| files | `allow` | `readonly string[]` | `["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", "**/*.json", "**/*.md", "**/*.css", ".moku/**"]` | Globs a file must match to be read or written. Case-sensitive. Not empty. |
| files | `deny` | `readonly string[]` | `["**/node_modules/**", "**/.git/**", "**/dist/**", "**/.env*"]` | Globs never listed, read or written. Case-insensitive. |
| files | `project` | `boolean` | `true` | Open the project index of `root` on start. `false` leaves it off with reason `"disabled"`; the index is never loaded. |
| hub | `path` | `string` | `"/__editor"` | URL prefix of every editor route. Starts with `/`; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `/`; no trailing or double slash. |
| hub | `allowOrigins` | `readonly string[]` | `[]` | Extra exact http(s) origins allowed to upgrade and call same-origin routes. No path, no trailing slash. |
| hub | `callTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Deadline of a forwarded call before -32002. Integer ≥ 100. |
| hub | `silentAfterMs` | `number` | `6000` | No heartbeat this long → silent. 65 s after a `paused: true` beat. Integer ≥ 100. |
| pages | `title` | `string` | `"moku editor"` | Tools page `<title>` and `ToolsBoot.title`. 1–120 characters. |
| pages | `editorUrl` | `string` | `"vscode://file/{path}:{line}"` | "Open in editor" template. Must contain `{path}`; scheme cannot be `javascript`, `data`, `vbscript`. |
| pages | `pageDir` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | Built page folder. `undefined` tries `dist/tools` next to the bundled module, then the repo `dist/tools`. |
| pages | `gameUrl` | `string` | `"/"` | Same-origin URL of the game page. Starts with `/`, not `//`, no `\`. |

### Tools

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| link | `retryMs` | `number` | `1000` | Base of the reconnect backoff `min(retryMs × 2^n, 8000)`. |
| link | `boot` | `string` | `"#moku-editor-boot"` | CSS selector of the boot JSON tag `pages` injects. |
| link | `reloadGraceMs` | `number` | `8000` | How long an expected reload (U7: close 1012, a reload the editor started, a game that said bye) reads `lost` with `reloading: true`. Without a heartbeat of the game by then the status is a plain `lost`. Positive; `onInit` throws `[moku-editor] link.reloadGraceMs is invalid.` otherwise. |
| workspace | `defaultWorkspace` | `WorkspaceId` | `"game"` | Shown at start when the URL hash names none. |
| workspace | `storageKey` | `string` | `"moku-editor"` | localStorage key of the preferences record. |
| workspace | `reloadTimeoutMs` | `number` | `15000` | How long `reload()` waits for the new session. |
| workspace | `hotReloadWaitMs` | `number` | `1500` | After a save with Bun hot reload on: how long `gameFrame().reload()` waits for the page Bun reloads before it reloads the frame itself. Positive. |
| workspace | `toastMs` | `number` | `2600` | How long one toast stays; hover or focus pauses it. |
| panels | — | `Record<string, never>` | `{}` | No options. |
| flowView | `historyLast` | `number` | `20` | Entries of `game.history` the panel watches. |
| flowView | `trailLength` | `number` | `6` | Edges drawn as the trail. |
| flowView | `rejectedOutcomes` | `readonly string[]` | `["rejected"]` | Outcomes drawn as rejections. |
| flowView | `styleSaveDelayMs` | `number` | `600` | Debounce of a style stepper burst. |
| flowView | `layout.file` | `string` | `".moku/editor/layout.json"` | Saved positions. |
| flowView | `layout.worker` | `boolean` | `true` | Run ELK in a Blob Web Worker; `false` runs it inline. |
| flowView | `layout.saveDelayMs` | `number` | `400` | Debounce of the layout save after a drop. |
| flowView | `zoom.min` | `number` | `0.08` | Lowest zoom. |
| flowView | `zoom.max` | `number` | `3` | Highest zoom. |
| flowView | `zoom.defaultMin` | `number` | `0.8` | Floor of the default camera. |
| flowView | `hub.minOutcomes` | `number` | `6` | Hub rule: a rest node with at least this many outcomes. |
| flowView | `hub.minReturns` | `number` | `4` | Hub rule: at least this many other nodes return to it. |
| gameView | `capturesDir` | `string` | `".moku/captures"` | Screenshots, series and the two pictures of a pick (`<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg`, `f<frame>-full.jpg`), each in a day folder `<yyyy-mm-dd>/` (local date; a Shot is `<hhmm>-<flow>.jpg`, a series `series-<hhmm>/`). `.moku/captures` or a folder under it (the files sandbox); `onInit` throws `[moku-editor] gameView.capturesDir must be .moku/captures or a folder under it.` otherwise. |
| gameView | `captureCardMs` | `number` | `10000` | Capture card hides after this unless hovered or focused. |
| gameView | `seriesDurationsMs` | `readonly number[]` | `[1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000]` | Duration chips. |
| gameView | `seriesIntervalsMs` | `readonly number[]` | `[16, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000]` | Interval chips. |
| gameView | `seriesWarnShots` | `number` | `200` | Popover warns above this many planned shots. |
| renderView | `fpsSamples` | `number` | `60` | FPS samples kept for the sparkline. |
| renderView | `releaseLogMax` | `number` | `50` | Release log entries kept. |
| stateView | `expandDepth` | `number` | `2` | Tree levels open by default. |
| stateView | `maxPatches` | `number` | `200` | Most patches kept per commit. |
| stateView | `pageSize` | `number` | `100` | Children shown per array or object before "Show N more". |
| filesView | `maxFiles` | `number` | `5000` | Most files the tree walk indexes. |
| filesView | `maxHighlightChars` | `number` | `512000` | Longer files show without colour. |
| filesView | `reloadExtensions` | `readonly string[]` | `[".ts", ".tsx", ".css", ".json"]` | A save of these outside `.moku/` runs the D-07 reload. |
| filesView | `revalidateMs` | `number` | `2000` | A clean tab is re-read on activation when older than this. |
| consoleView | `maxLines` | `number` | `5000` | Most lines kept; oldest go first. |
| consoleView | `preserveLog` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial state of Preserve log. |
| consoleView | `freshMs` | `number` | `1200` | Highlight time of a fresh error row. |
| consoleView | `summaryChars` | `number` | `160` | Characters of non-string `data` shown inline. |

### Bin

```
moku-editor [--root DIR] [--preload FILE]… [--serve-plugin FILE]… [--port 3000] [--no-hmr]
moku-editor <game-html> [--port 3000] [--root .] [--no-hmr] [--help]
moku-editor mcp [<game-html>] [--port N] [--root DIR] [--no-hmr]
moku-editor mcp-config [<game-html>] [--port N]
moku-editor e2e -c <playwright config> [playwright args…]
```

| Flag | Short | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--port` | `-p` | `3000` | Digits, 0–65535. `0` picks a free port. |
| `--root` | `-r` | `.` | Project root the editor reads and writes; the moku-game folder of the engine page. Not empty. |
| `--no-hmr` | | hot reload on | Serves with `development: { hmr: false, console: true }`; `hotReload()` reports `{ hmr: false, owner: "bin" }`. |
| `--preload` | | none | A file Bun preloads in the serving process. Repeatable. Engine page only. |
| `--serve-plugin` | | none | A Bun plugin the engine page bundles with, after the engine's hot plugin. Repeatable. Engine page only. |
| `--help` | `-h` | | Prints usage, exit 0. |

Engine page (B5, D-49 … D-51; keys watch D-54, D-55): without an html file the bin serves a moku-game folder (`index.ts` + `config.ts`). (0) Checked first: without the real process (`deps.reexec`, unit seams): "[moku-editor] the engine page needs the real process: pass the game HTML file", exit 1. (1) Not a moku-game folder: "[moku-editor] <root> has no index.ts and config.ts: pass the game HTML file, or run in a moku-game folder", exit 2. (2) It imports `@moku-labs/game/cli` as the game root resolves it, once, for `preparePage` and `watchKeys` (both required, D-54); when it does not resolve or lacks either: "[moku-editor] @moku-labs/game/cli does not resolve from <root>: install @moku-labs/game >=0.13.1 in the game", exit 1. (3) `preparePage(root, { agents: ["@moku-labs/editor/agent/page"], preload, servePlugins })`, the flag paths resolved against the cwd; a throw prints the engine's `[game] …` text, exit 1. (4) From an editor working tree (its package root, found from `Bun.main`, is not under `realpath(<root>)/node_modules` and has `scripts/tree/bundle.ts`) that plugin is appended to `servePlugins`: `@moku-labs/editor`, `/agent`, `/agent/page` and `/tools` bundle from the tree's `dist/`, whose imports of the engine, Pixi, core, common and preact are rewritten in `onLoad` to the game's copies (never `onResolve`, demos#46). (5) Keys watch (D-54, D-55): the parent bin calls `watchKeys(root, { onError })` of the same cli import. It resolves after the engine's first scan, so `generated/` is fresh before the child serves; later a save of an asset or of a `strings/<locale>.json` scans again. A failed scan, the first one too, is one warning (`ui.warn` with the engine's message) and the bin keeps running. A rejection prints the engine's `[game] …` text, exit 1, and no child is spawned. The html form never watches keys; the child never imports the engine's cli. (6) The bin always re-runs itself (D-51): `[execPath, "--config=<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml", Bun.main, "<root>/.moku/index.html", "--root", root, "--port", port, "--no-hmr"?]`, `cwd: root`, `MOKU_EDITOR_REEXEC=1`, signals forwarded, the parent exits with the child's code. The keys watch is closed in a `finally` around the child, so it stops with the child; a throw of `close()` is one warning. Before the spawn the parent has no signal handlers of its own (`main` installs the early ones only with an html file): a SIGINT or SIGTERM while the page is written or the first scan runs ends it with the default action, exit 130 or 143, no child is spawned, and the keys watch ends with the process. The child serves that html as any re-spawned bin; the discovery file's `html` is `<root>/.moku/index.html`. `--preload` and `--serve-plugin` with an html file: "--preload and --serve-plugin need the engine page: drop the html file"; on `mcp` and `mcp-config`: "--preload and --serve-plugin belong to the serving bin". The MCP launcher restarts a gone engine bin in the engine form (no html), so the page is written again and served under that bunfig. Limit: `--preload` and `--serve-plugin` are not in the discovery file, so the restarted bin has none.

Hot reload (D-23, round 2 R6): by default the bin serves with `development: { hmr: true, console: true }` and calls `pages.attachServer(options)` right after `Bun.serve`. A save of a game source makes Bun reload the game page; before it reloads, the bridge stores a `game.bookmark` checkpoint in `sessionStorage`, and the new page restores it (and pauses again when it was paused) and says so in its hello (`manifest.restored`). Bun 1.3.14 cannot switch HMR on a running server, so the bin gives `attachServer` its restart and the Hot reload switch restarts the server with HMR flipped on the same port (D-32): `POST {P}/hmr` answers 200 with the asked state, then the server restarts (A1); the token, the sessions table and `.moku/editor.json` stay, every socket drops for about a second, and the tools page reloads the game frame with its checkpoint so the page gains or drops `/_bun/client`. While HMR is off a save on disk does not reload the game. A failed restart publishes the old state and serves the old options again. Before the restart serves with HMR on, the bin waits, at most 5 s, until Bun's bundler is idle (D-57): Bun 1.3.14 freezes its main thread, or crashes, when the page rebundle of the server without HMR (Bun starts one on every page request) and the dev server's first bundle run at once, and a page request that reaches the old server during the switch sets that up. Hot swap (game 0.5.0): with `[serve.static] plugins = ["@moku-labs/game/hot"]` in the game root's `bunfig.toml`, a save of a view module (`.tsx`, `styles.ts`, `view.ts`, `animations.ts`, `effects.ts`, `generated/strings.<locale>.ts`) swaps in place: same session, no reload, toast "Game updated"; a logic module still reloads and restores. Bun reads that bunfig once at process start from the process cwd, so a `run` whose `--root` has a `[serve.static]` bunfig and whose cwd is another folder re-spawns the bin in the root (`reexec.ts`: absolute html and root, `MOKU_EDITOR_REEXEC=1` loop guard, SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP forwarded, the parent exits with the child's code, the discovery file names the child). The MCP launcher spawns the bin with `cwd: root`.

e2e (D-52, D-53, `e2e.ts`): one Playwright process, so one fresh editor bin, per project and spec file, because Bun's dev server degrades after many hot reloads in one process (also within one project: merge-game failed from the ~90th reload-heavy spec). `splitRest(rest)` sorts the user's words into `projects` (`--project X Y…` takes every next word not starting with `-`, as Playwright's variadic option, up to a path-like word (a `/`, or `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.mjs` at the end), which is a file filter, so a project named like a path needs `--project=X`; `--project=X` one), `files` (any other word not starting with `-` that is not a flag's value), `reporters` (`--reporter`, `--add-reporter`), `listOnly` (`--shard`, `--last-failed`) and `other`; a flag with a required value (`-g`, `-G`, `-j`, `--repeat-each`, `--timeout`, …) keeps its next word, `-u` / `--update-snapshots` only `all|changed|missing|none`, `--debug` only `inspector|cli`, `--only-changed` a word not starting with `-` and not ending in `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`; `--flag=v` is one word. The plan comes from `bun x playwright test -c <config> --list --reporter=json --pass-with-no-tests <files> --project=<p>… <other> <listOnly>` (JSON output env vars removed; a failed or unparsable list: "[moku-editor] could not list the tests of <config>: <reason>", exit 1). `listPlan(json)` answers `{ rootDir: config.rootDir, pairs }`: one (project, file) pair per named project and spec file with at least one listed test, projects in config order, files in list order (`specs[].file`, relative to `rootDir`), unnamed projects skipped. Each pair runs as `bun x playwright test -c <config> --project=<p> <fileFilter(file, rootDir)> --pass-with-no-tests <other> <reporters>` with `PORT` = `PORT` (an integer 1-65535, else 4417) + its index, one after another, all of them; `fileFilter` = `^<rootDir>/<file>$`, regex-escaped with `/` separators (Playwright tests a file argument as a regex on the absolute path). `--project=<p>` is one word because the variadic `--project <p>` would read the file regex as a project. After each run `ui.info("<project> · <file> · passed|failed (code N) · <s> s")`, at the end `ui.info("e2e: <n> runs · <failed> failed · <s> s")` (`E2eDeps.now`, default `performance.now`). A failed run's line and a failing summary print as errors; a warning names the tests of an unnamed project that did not run. Exit = the first non-zero code, else 0. A `--list`, an empty plan (no test matched, or only an unnamed project) runs once as given, without `--pass-with-no-tests`, so Playwright's "No tests found" tells the user. Lock (`E2eDeps.lock`: `take(): Promise<number | undefined>`, `release(): Promise<void>`; `processE2eDeps` sets `fileLock(process.cwd())`): before the CI install `runE2e` creates `.moku/e2e.lock` in the cwd with the bin's pid (`wx`, folder created); while a live pid (`process.kill(pid, 0)`) holds it: "[moku-editor] another e2e run (pid N) holds .moku/e2e.lock: wait for it, or delete the file when no run is left", exit 1, nothing runs; a dead or unreadable pid is taken over; released in a `finally` after the last run, also after a failure, and only while the file holds this pid; a `--list` takes no lock. `CI=true` runs `bun x playwright install chromium` first. Only `-c X` / `--config X` / `--config=X` is read, before `--help` (missing: "[moku-editor] e2e needs the Playwright config: -c <file>", exit 2); no signal handlers, a Ctrl+C reaches Playwright through the process group.

Exit codes: 0 help, `mcp-config`, `mcp` after stdin ended or a SIGINT/SIGTERM, or serving; the child's code after a re-spawn or the engine page's re-run; 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) when the engine form gets the signal before its child is spawned, no child; 1 missing or bad HTML file, start failed, port in use, the engine page not written or its keys watch not started; 2 bad arguments, or no html file and a root that is not a moku-game folder. Binds 127.0.0.1 only; the token is never printed.

Discovery file: after `Bun.serve` the bin writes `<root>/.moku/editor.json` `{ version: 1, pid, port, url, ws, token, root, html, startedAt }` (type `EditorDiscovery`, mode 0600, temp file then rename) and removes it on SIGINT/SIGTERM and in an `exit` listener, only while it still carries this pid. A bin killed with SIGKILL leaves it; the MCP bridge treats a dead pid as no bin. Add `.moku/` to the game's `.gitignore`.

`mcp-config` prints the `.mcp.json` snippet, a blank line and the `claude mcp add` line, then exits 0:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "moku-editor": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "bunx",
      "args": ["moku-editor", "mcp", "web/index.html", "--port", "3000"]
    }
  }
}

claude mcp add moku-editor -- bunx moku-editor mcp web/index.html --port 3000
```

MCP bridge (`moku-editor mcp`, `src/plugins/pages/mcp/`, D-31): a separate process, not a plugin; a hub **tools client** (`${ws}?token=…&kind=tools`, `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>`), so the hub's session choice, input checks and files sandbox apply as for the tools page. Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio; stdout carries only protocol frames, logs go to stderr.

- `initialize` → `{ protocolVersion, capabilities: { tools: { listChanged: true }, logging: {} }, serverInfo: { name: "moku-editor", version }, instructions }` (`instructions`: which tools are generic, which are command doors, that cheat_* and raw_* change the game outside its rules, and that the list changes when the game reloads); versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` (the client's when listed, else `2025-11-25`). `ping` and `logging/setLevel` → `{}`. An unknown method → -32601, bad params → -32602, a line that is not JSON → -32700. Notifications are never answered; `notifications/cancelled { requestId }` aborts that call. `notifications/progress` during `moku_wait` and `moku_series` when the request has `_meta.progressToken`; `notifications/tools/list_changed` only when the door tools change (below); a change before `notifications/initialized` is sent once right after it. `tools/list` is the generic tools, then the door tools; the first one waits at most 3 s for the door tools. A door tool that is gone answers `isError` "`<name>` is gone: the game changed. Call moku_manifest, or moku_run { id }."
- Claude Code 2.1.280 (recorded in `src/plugins/pages/__tests__/fixtures/claude-*.json`): it sends `server/discover` (draft protocol 2026-07-28) first, gets -32601, then `initialize` with `protocolVersion: "2025-11-25"` and id 0, `notifications/initialized` and `tools/list`.
- Which bin: a live `.moku/editor.json` under `--root` (default the working directory) wins. Without one the bridge starts `moku-editor <html> --port <port> --root <root> [--no-hmr]` detached (output in `.moku/editor.log`, 0600), when it knows a game html (argv, else the last discovery file it saw); the html `<root>/.moku/index.html` (the engine page) is left out, so the bin starts in the engine form `moku-editor --port <port> --root <root> [--no-hmr]` and re-runs under `--config=<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml` (D-51); port `--port`, else the last port, else 3000; it waits at most 15 s for the discovery file and owns that bin. Without an html, tools answer `isError` "moku-editor is not running. Start it (`bunx moku-editor web/index.html --port 3000`) or call moku_start." A closed hub socket is re-read and reconnected once.
- Teardown on stdin end, SIGINT or SIGTERM (the same steps): pending calls are aborted, every watch is dropped, the socket closes, an owned bin gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s; a bin the bridge did not start keeps running. After a signal it lets go of stdin, so the process exits 0 while the client keeps the pipe open.
